react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms (RaMP multi-DB ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and mummichog m/z-direct) converge on a single dominant biological signal: the Galactose Metabolism pathway (KEGG:hsa00052) is the unanimous cross-paradigm winner. In the RaMP merged-database ORA this pathway shares rank 2 with KEGG:hsa00052 and rank 1 with SMPDB:SMP00043, achieving an extraordinary FDR of 1.22e-15 (fold enrichment 1 743×) and hitting all five structurally reconciled input metabolites — galactinol (C01235), sucrose (C00089), myo-inositol (C00137), galactitol (C01697), and glycerol (C00116) — across a 31-member pathway roster. The MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA confirms this with a raw p-value of 9.53e-10 (rank 1, 5/27 metabolites hit). The mummichog m/z-direct analysis independently recovers galactose metabolism in rank 4 (p = 2.52e-04) with an even more expansive metabolite set, and additionally recovers phosphatidylinositol phosphate metabolism (rank 3, p = 8.40e-05) as a second coherent network module driven by myo-inositol (C00137) and glycerol (C00116). Acetylcholine (C01996) is recovered only in the mummichog glycerophospholipid node; the 2,3-epoxyaflatoxin B1 (C19586) does not appear in any pathway result, indicating it falls below detection thresholds across all paradigms — likely reflecting limited compound coverage for this mycotoxin metabolite in the reference networks. Glycerol is the sole compound shared across the galactose and glycerophospholipid/glycerophospholipid metabolic nodes, acting as a structural bridge between sugar and membrane-lipid homeostasis. The convergent evidence across ORA and network-diffusion paradigms identifies galactose metabolism as the primary affected pathway, with myo-inositol and glycerol serving as key driver metabolites linking carbohydrate flux to phospholipid signalling.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms — RaMP multi-database ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and mummichog m/z-direct — converge on Galactose Metabolism (KEGG:map00052 / KEGG:hsa00052) as the dominant affected pathway. In RaMP merged-database ORA, Galactose Metabolism shares top rank (rank 2) with Galactosemia (SMPDB:SMP00182), driven by five input metabolites: galactinol (KEGG:C01235), sucrose (KEGG:C00089), myo-inositol (KEGG:C00137), galactitol (KEGG:C01697), and glycerol (KEGG:C00116), with an FDR of 1.22e-15. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently confirms KEGG:hsa00052 with a raw p-value of 9.53e-10, hitting 5 out of 27 pathway metabolites. Mummichog recovers Galactose metabolism (MUMM:galactose_metabolism) at rank 3 with p = 7.56e-04, and independently recovers Phosphatidylinositol phosphate metabolism (MUMM:phosphatidylinositol_phosphate_metabolism) at rank 2 with p = 8.40e-05, with myo-inositol and glycerol as the shared driver metabolites linking carbohydrate flux to phospholipid signalling. Acetylcholine (KEGG:C01996) maps only to the mummichog glycerophospholipid node. 2,3-Epoxyaflatoxin B1 (KEGG:C19586) is not recovered by any enrichment paradigm.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three pathway-enrichment paradigms (RaMP multi-database ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and mummichog m/z-direct analysis) converge on Galactose Metabolism as the dominant affected pathway. RaMP reports Galactose Metabolism (SMPDB:SMP00043) and its closely related disease map Galactosemia (SMPDB:SMP00182) both at rank 0-1 with an FDR of 1.22e-15, covering five input metabolites (galactinol, sucrose, myo-inositol, galactitol, glycerol) out of 31 pathway members. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently confirms the same KEGG identifier (KEGG:hsa00052, the native KEGG namespace for Galactose Metabolism) at rank 0 with p = 9.533e-10, hitting 5 out of 27 pathway metabolites (galactinol, sucrose, galactitol, glycerol, myo-inositol). Mummichog recovers Galactose metabolism (MUMM:galactose_metabolism) at rank 3 with p = 0.00109. The five shared driver metabolites span the Leloir pathway intermediates and the sugar-alcohol branch: galactinol (KEGG:C01235) as the alpha-D-galactosyl-(1->3)-1D-myo-inositol donor, sucrose (KEGG:C00089) as a source of free galactose, myo-inositol (KEGG:C00137) as both product and precursor for inositol phosphate signaling, galactitol (KEGG:C01697) as the sorbitol-group reduced product, and glycerol (KEGG:C00116) linking galactose catabolism into glycerophospholipid biosynthesis. Glycerophospholipid metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-1483257) is supported by RaMP at rank 8 with glycerol as the shared compound, and independently by mummichog (MUMM:glycerophospholipid_metabolism, rank 4, p = 0.00252). Acetylcholine (KEGG:C01996) maps to the MUMM:glycerophospholipid_metabolism node via the sn-glycero-3-phosphate backbone, while 2,3-epoxyaflatoxin B1 (KEGG:C19586) is not recovered by any enrichment paradigm.

FELLA R subprocess errored at runtime (currently 'argument is of length zero' on every sub6b-v3 task — W9 D4 stretch target); skip the network/diffusion paradigm and rely on ORA + mummichog
use run_ramp_enrichment (multi-DB ORA, broader namespace coverage) or run_metaboanalystr_psea (KEGG-specific ORA) instead
